verses.1:1: Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to the chosen sojourners of the dispersion in Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia,
verses.1:2: according to the foreknowledge of God the Father, for the sanctification of the Spirit, for obedience and the sprinkling of the blood of Jesus Christ. Grace and peace be multiplied to you.
verses.1:3: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who according to His great mercy regenerated us into a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead,
verses.1:4: into an inheritance incorruptible, undefiled, and unfading, preserved in the heavens in you,
verses.1:5: who are guarded in the power of God through faith for salvation, ready to be revealed in the last time.
verses.1:6: In this you will exult, if for a little while now it is necessary to be grieved in various trials,
verses.1:7: so that the testing of your faith, much more precious than gold (which is tested through fire), may be found for praise and glory and honor at the revelation of Jesus Christ,
verses.1:8: whom, though you have not seen Him, you love; in whom, not seeing Him even now, you believe; and believing, you will exult with inexpressible and glorified joy,
verses.1:9: obtaining the goal of your faith, the salvation of souls.
verses.1:10: Concerning this salvation, the prophets who prophesied about the grace to come in you inquired carefully and searched,
verses.1:11: searching into what or what kind of time the Spirit of Christ in them was indicating, foretelling those sufferings that are in Christ and the subsequent glories,
verses.1:12: to whom it was revealed that it was not to themselves, but to you, that they were ministering those things which have now been announced to you through those who proclaimed the gospel to you, with the Holy Spirit sent from heaven, upon whom angels desire to look.
verses.1:13: For this reason, with the loins of your mind girded, being sober, hope completely in the grace that is offered to you at the revelation of Jesus Christ,
verses.1:14: as children of obedience, not conformed to the former desires of your ignorance,
verses.1:15: but according to Him who called you, the Holy One, you yourselves also be holy in all conduct,
verses.1:16: because it is written, "You will be holy, because I am holy."
verses.1:17: And if you call upon Him as Father who judges without partiality according to each one's work, conduct yourselves in fear during the time of your sojourning,
verses.1:18: knowing that you were redeemed not with corruptible things, gold or silver, from your futile conduct of ancestral tradition,
verses.1:19: but with the precious blood of Christ, as of an unblemished and undefiled lamb,
verses.1:20: foreknown indeed before the foundation of the world, yet manifested in the last times for your sake,
verses.1:21: who through Him are believers in God, who raised Him from the dead and gave Him glory, so that your faith and hope might be in God.
verses.1:22: Purifying your souls in the obedience of love, in love of the brotherhood, love one another more earnestly from a sincere heart,
verses.1:23: having been born again not from corruptible seed, but incorruptible, through the word of the living God, who endures forever;
verses.1:24: for all flesh is like grass, and all its glory is like the flower of grass; the grass has withered, and its flower has fallen.
verses.1:25: But the word of the Lord remains forever. And this is the word that was proclaimed as the gospel to you.
verses.2:1: Laying aside therefore all malice, and all deceit, and pretenses, and envies, and all slanders,
verses.2:2: like newborn infants, long for the reasonable milk without deceit, so that by it you may grow into salvation,
verses.2:3: if indeed you have tasted that the Lord is sweet.
verses.2:4: Coming to Him, a living stone, rejected indeed by men, yet chosen and honored by God,
verses.2:5: you yourselves also, like living stones, are being built up, a spiritual house, a holy priesthood, to offer spiritual sacrifices, acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.
verses.2:6: For this reason Scripture contains this: "Look, I am laying in Zion a chief cornerstone, chosen, precious; and the one who believes in Him will not be put to shame."
verses.2:7: To you therefore who believe belongs the honor; but to those who do not believe, the stone that the builders rejected, this has become the head of the corner,
verses.2:8: and a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense to those who stumble at the word and do not believe, for which they were also appointed.
verses.2:9: But you are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people of possession, so that you may announce the virtues of Him who called you out of darkness into His wonderful light.
verses.2:10: You who once were not a people, yet now are the people of God; who had not obtained mercy, yet now have obtained mercy.
verses.2:11: Beloved, I implore you as sojourners and foreigners to abstain from fleshly desires, which wage war against the soul,
verses.2:12: keeping your conduct good among the Gentiles, so that in the matter in which they slander you as evildoers, observing you from your good works, they may glorify God on the day of visitation.
verses.2:13: Be subject therefore to every human creature for God's sake, whether to the king as preeminent,
verses.2:14: or to governors as sent by him for the punishment of evildoers, yet for the praise of the good;
verses.2:15: for such is the will of God, that by doing good you may silence the ignorance of foolish men,
verses.2:16: as free, and not having freedom as a covering for malice, but as servants of God.
verses.2:17: Honor all people; love the brotherhood; fear God; hold the king in honor.
verses.2:18: Servants, be subject in all fear to your masters, not only to the good and gentle, but also to the harsh.
verses.2:19: For this is grace, if because of conscience toward God someone endures sorrows, suffering unjustly.
verses.2:20: For what glory is it if, sinning and being beaten, you endure it? But if, doing good, you endure patiently, this is grace before God.
verses.2:21: For to this you were called, because Christ also suffered for us, leaving you an example so that you may follow His footsteps,
verses.2:22: who committed no sin, nor was deceit found in His mouth;
verses.2:23: who, when He was reviled, did not revile; when He suffered, He did not threaten, but handed Himself over to the one judging Him unjustly;
verses.2:24: who Himself bore our sins in His body upon the tree, so that, dead to sins, we might live to righteousness; by whose bruise you were healed.
verses.2:25: For you were like straying sheep, yet now you have turned back to the shepherd and overseer of your souls.
verses.3:1: Likewise also, let wives be subject to their husbands, so that even if any do not believe the word, they may be won without a word through the conduct of the wives,
verses.3:2: observing your chaste conduct in fear.
verses.3:3: Let theirs not be the outward styling of hair, or the putting on of gold, or the adornment of wearing garments,
verses.3:4: but the hidden person of the heart, in the incorruptibility of a quiet and gentle spirit, which is rich in the sight of God.
verses.3:5: For in this way formerly the holy women also, hoping in God, adorned themselves, being subject to their own husbands,
verses.3:6: just as Sarah obeyed Abraham, calling him lord, whose daughters you are, doing good and not fearing any alarm.
verses.3:7: Husbands, likewise, live together according to knowledge, imparting honor to the female vessel as the weaker one, as also to fellow heirs of the grace of life, so that your prayers may not be hindered.
verses.3:8: Finally, all of you be of one mind, sympathetic, lovers of the brotherhood, merciful, gentle, humble,
verses.3:9: not returning evil for evil, nor reviling for reviling, but on the contrary blessing, because to this you were called, so that you may possess a blessing by inheritance.
verses.3:10: For the one who wants to love life and to see good days, let him restrain his tongue from evil, and let his lips not speak deceit.
verses.3:11: Let him turn aside from evil and do good; let him seek peace and pursue it,
verses.3:12: because the eyes of the Lord are upon the righteous, and His ears are toward their prayers; yet the face of the Lord is upon those who do evil things.
verses.3:13: And who is there who would harm you, if you are eager followers of what is good?
verses.3:14: But even if you suffer anything for the sake of righteousness, you are blessed. And do not fear their fear, and do not be troubled.
verses.3:15: But sanctify the Lord Christ in your hearts, ready at all times to give a satisfactory answer to everyone asking you for a reason about that hope which is in you;
verses.3:16: yet with gentleness and fear, having a good conscience, so that in the matter in which they slander you, those who falsely accuse your good conduct in Christ may be put to shame.
verses.3:17: For it is better (if the will of God should will it) to suffer doing good than doing evil.
verses.3:18: Because Christ also died once for our sins, the righteous for the unrighteous, so that He might offer us to God, put to death indeed in the flesh, yet made alive in the spirit,
verses.3:19: in which He also came and preached to those spirits who were in prison,
verses.3:20: who had once been unbelieving, when they waited for the patience of God in the days of Noah, while the ark was being built, in which a few, that is, eight souls, were saved through water.
verses.3:21: And of like form to this, baptism has now saved you also, not the putting away of the filth of the flesh, but the inquiry of a good conscience toward God, through the resurrection of Jesus Christ,
verses.3:22: who is at the right hand of God, swallowing up death so that we might be made heirs of eternal life, having gone into heaven with angels and authorities and powers made subject to Him.
verses.4:1: Since Christ therefore suffered in the flesh, arm yourselves also with the same mindset, because the one who has suffered in the flesh has ceased from sins,
verses.4:2: so that he may live the remaining time in the flesh no longer for the desires of men, but for the will of God.
verses.4:3: For the time that has passed is sufficient to accomplish the will of the Gentiles, for those who have walked in debaucheries, desires, bouts of drunkenness, revelries, drinking parties, and unlawful worship of idols.
verses.4:4: At this they are astonished when you do not run along with them into the same confusion of debauchery, and they blaspheme.
verses.4:5: They will render an account to Him who is prepared to judge the living and the dead.
verses.4:6: For because of this the gospel has been proclaimed even to the dead, so that they may indeed be judged according to men in the flesh, yet live according to God in the spirit.
verses.4:7: Now the end of all things has drawn near. Be prudent, therefore, and keep watch in prayers.
verses.4:8: Now above all, maintain constant mutual love among yourselves, because love covers over a multitude of sins.
verses.4:9: Be hospitable toward one another without grumbling.
verses.4:10: Just as each one has received grace, administer it to one another as good stewards of the multifaceted grace of God.
verses.4:11: If anyone speaks, let it be as the utterances of God; if anyone serves, let it be as from the power that God supplies, so that in all things God may be honored through Jesus Christ, to whom belong glory and sovereignty forever and ever. Amen.
verses.4:12: Beloved, do not feel like strangers in the burning heat that comes upon you for testing, as though something new were happening to you,
verses.4:13: but sharing in the sufferings of Christ, rejoice, so that in the revelation of His glory also you may rejoice exultantly.
verses.4:14: If you are reproached in the name of Christ, you will be blessed, because what is of the honor, glory, and power of God, and He who is His Spirit, rests upon you.
verses.4:15: But let none of you suffer as a murderer, or a thief, or a slanderer, or one who covets what belongs to others.
verses.4:16: Yet if as a Christian, let him not be ashamed, but let him glorify God in this name,
verses.4:17: because it is time for judgment to begin with the house of God. Now if it begins first with us, what will be the end of those who do not believe the gospel of God?
verses.4:18: And if the righteous one will barely be saved, where will the ungodly and the sinner appear?
verses.4:19: Therefore let those also who suffer according to the will of God commit their souls to the faithful Creator in good deeds.
verses.5:1: Therefore I urge the elders who are among you, as a fellow elder and witness of the sufferings of Christ, and also a sharer in that glory which is to be revealed in the future:
verses.5:2: shepherd the flock of God that is among you, exercising oversight not under compulsion, but of your own accord according to God; not for the sake of shameful gain, but willingly;
verses.5:3: and not as domineering over the allotted portions, but becoming a model for the flock from the heart.
verses.5:4: And when the chief of shepherds appears, you will obtain the unfading crown of glory.
verses.5:5: Likewise, young men, be subject to the elders. And all of you, instill humility in one another, because God resists the proud, but to the humble He gives grace.
verses.5:6: Humble yourselves, therefore, under the powerful hand of God, so that He may exalt you in the time of visitation,
verses.5:7: casting all your worry upon Him, because He Himself cares about you.
verses.5:8: Be sober, and keep watch, because your adversary the devil goes around like a roaring lion, looking for someone to devour.
verses.5:9: Resist him, strong in faith, knowing that the same suffering is happening to your brotherhood that is in the world.
verses.5:10: Now the God of all grace, who called us into His eternal glory in Christ Jesus, will Himself perfect, confirm, and establish us after we have suffered a little.
verses.5:11: To Him be glory and sovereignty forever and ever. Amen.
verses.5:12: Through Silvanus, a faithful brother to you, as I judge, I have written briefly, urging and testifying that this is the true grace of God, in which you stand.
verses.5:13: The church that is in Babylon, chosen together with you, greets you, and so does Mark, my son.
verses.5:14: Greet one another with a holy kiss. Grace to all of you who are in Christ Jesus. Amen.

notes.1:4: The Vulgate reads "in vobis" (ablative, "in you"; cf. 1:10), reflecting a Latin rendering of Greek "eis hymas" ("for you").
notes.1:6: The Vulgate "exsultabis" is second-person singular future ("you [sg.] will exult"), shifting briefly from the plural verbs around it (cf. "exsultabitis" in 1:8).
notes.1:11: The Vulgate reads "in Christo" ("in Christ"), differing from the Greek "eis Christon" ("for/destined for Christ").
notes.1:12: The Vulgate reads "in quem" (masculine singular, referring to the Holy Spirit), differing from the Greek neuter plural "eis ha" ("into which things").
notes.1:22: The Vulgate reads "in obedientia caritatis" ("in the obedience of love"), differing from the Greek "en te hypakoe tes aletheias" ("in obedience to the truth").
notes.2:2: The Vulgate renders Greek "logikon" ("rational," "spiritual," or "of the word") as "rationabile" ("reasonable"); in 2:3, "dulcis" ("sweet") corresponds to Greek "chrestos" ("good/kind").
notes.2:13: The Vulgate reads "omni humanae creaturae" ("every human creature") and "propter Deum" ("for God's sake"), whereas the Greek has "every human institution/creation" and "for the Lord's sake".
notes.2:20: The Vulgate reads the adverb "patienter" ("patiently"), differing from the Greek participle "paschontes" ("suffering").
notes.2:21: The Vulgate shifts pronouns from first-person "pro nobis" ("for us") to second-person "vobis" ("leaving you").
notes.2:23: The Vulgate reading "judicanti se injuste" ("to the one judging Him unjustly") is a notable divergence from the Greek "to krinonti dikaios" ("to Him who judges justly").
notes.3:1: The Clementine text prints "per mulierem conversationem" (accusative singular, a traditional textual variant for genitive plural "mulierum", "of the wives").
notes.3:8: The Vulgate lists six qualities, including both "modesti" ("gentle") and "humiles" ("humble"), where the Greek text lists five.
notes.3:18: The Vulgate uses the sacrificial verb "offerret" ("offer") for Greek "prosagage" ("bring"); lowercase "spiritu" (parallel to "carne") may refer either to Christ's spirit or to the Holy Spirit.
notes.3:20: The Vulgate reads "quando exspectabant Dei patientiam" ("when they waited for the patience of God") with a plural verb, differing from the Greek "when the patience of God waited".
notes.3:22: The Vulgate adds "deglutiens mortem ut vitae aeternae haeredes efficeremur" ("swallowing up death so that we might be made heirs of eternal life"), a distinctive Latin clause absent from the Greek text.
notes.4:3: The Vulgate uses a third-person dative construction, his qui ambulaverunt ("for those who have walked"), whereas the Greek text uses a participle referring to the readers ("you").
notes.4:4: The Vulgate noun confusionem ("confusion") renders Greek anachysin ("outpouring" or "flood").
notes.4:12: Latin nolite peregrinari in fervore literally means "do not be strangers in the burning heat," calquing the Greek verb xenizesthe ("be surprised" or "think strange"); similarly, novi ("new") renders Greek xenou ("strange").
notes.4:14: The Vulgate expands the subject to quod est honoris, gloriae, et virtutis Dei, et qui est ejus Spiritus ("what is of the honor, glory, and power of God, and He who is His Spirit"), whereas the Greek reads simply "the Spirit of glory and of God."
notes.4:15: Latin maledicus ("slanderer") and alienorum appetitor ("one who covets what belongs to others") are distinctly Vulgate renderings of Greek kakopoios ("evildoer") and allotriepiskopos ("meddler" or "busybody").
notes.5:3: Latin in cleris ("over the allotted portions") borrows Greek kleron ("allotments" or "heritages," the origin of English "clergy"); the closing phrase ex animo ("from the heart") is a Vulgate addition absent from the Greek text.
notes.5:5: Latin humilitatem insinuate ("instill humility," literally "bring into the bosom") translates Greek egkombosasthe ("clothe yourselves with").
notes.5:6: The Vulgate adds visitationis ("of visitation") to in tempore ("in the time"), whereas the standard Greek text reads simply "in due time."
notes.5:10: The Vulgate reads vocavit nos ("called us") rather than Greek "called you," and has three verbs (perficiet, confirmabit, solidabitque) where the critical Greek text has four.
notes.5:14: The Vulgate reads in osculo sancto ("with a holy kiss") instead of Greek "with a kiss of love," and Gratia ("Grace") instead of Greek "Peace."
